title: Balanced Brackets, Three Kinds
statement:
`(`, `[` and `{` each need to be closed by the matching `)`, `]` or `}` --
and closed in the right order: `([)]` is not balanced even though it has
one of each character, because the `[` opens *after* the `(` but closes
*before* it does. A `Stack<T>` is built for exactly this shape of problem:
the most recently opened bracket is always the first one that has to close.

## Your function

```
public static bool IsBalanced(string text);
```

`text` may contain any characters; only `(`, `)`, `[`, `]`, `{` and `}`
participate in the check, and every other character is ignored. Return
`true` if every closing bracket matches the type of the most recently
unclosed opening bracket, and no opening bracket is left unclosed at the
end.

## Watch out

- **`Stack<T>.Pop()` and `Stack<T>.Peek()` both throw
  `InvalidOperationException` on an empty stack.** A closing bracket that
  arrives with nothing open to match it -- `text` starts with `)`, say --
  has to be checked for *before* popping, not discovered by catching the
  exception popping raises.
- **A stack that is not empty at the end means something was opened and
  never closed.** `"(()"` never sees a closing bracket it disagrees with --
  every `)` it does see matches correctly -- so the mismatch can only be
  caught by checking the stack is empty once `text` is exhausted, not by
  anything that happens while consuming it.
- **The three bracket types do not interchange.** `"(]"` is unbalanced: `(`
  was opened, `]` arrives, and `]` closes a `[`, not a `(` -- popping the
  stack and finding the wrong opening character is exactly as much of a
  failure as finding no opening character at all.
